Six months with Tallybird: an honest review

I switched to Tallybird in March after years of juggling spreadsheets, and for most of that time I would have told anyone who asked that it was the best money app I'd ever used. So please read this whole review before you decide anything, because the ending matters.

First, the good parts, and there are a lot of them. The design is lovely: clean, calm and never cluttered, even with nine accounts connected. Linking all nine bank accounts took one attempt each, and for five months the overnight sync ran so quietly I forgot it existed. Setting up categories took about ten minutes, and the automatic categorisation got smarter every week; by May it was sorting almost all of my transactions correctly without any help. The monthly reports are the best I've seen in any app. I finally understood where our grocery money was going, and we cut that bill by almost a fifth over the spring. Shared budgets with my partner worked perfectly, and the goal tracker genuinely motivated us to pay off a car loan two months early. I've read other reviews complaining about crashes, but in six months I never had a single one, on my phone or my tablet.

There are small niggles. The widget only shows one budget at a time, the dark mode is more grey than dark, and I wish I could split a transaction into more than four parts. The web version also feels like an afterthought next to the phone app. None of that would have stopped me recommending it.

Now the part that matters. In late August, after an update, Tallybird's bank sync ran overnight and deleted every transaction from June, July and August across all nine of my accounts. Three months of categorised history, notes and receipt photos were simply gone. Nothing in the app warned me; I only noticed because the monthly report suddenly showed a summer with no spending at all. The balances were still right, which somehow made it more confusing. I contacted support the same morning. The first reply came eleven days later and asked me to try logging out and back in. By then I had already rebuilt what I could from bank statements.

I've since exported everything that was left and moved our budgeting back to a spreadsheet. I've cancelled my subscription and I won't be renewing. It's genuinely sad, because the app itself is beautifully made. But a budgeting app that can silently wipe three months of data, and a support team that takes eleven days to answer, isn't something I can trust with our finances.
